title: Laugh with, not at.
old_caption: A joke too early can feel like a dodge when someone is still hurt. Talk first, then let the inside joke come back. Laughing together is the sweet part after you're heard.

title: Plan the next one calm.
old_caption: The best time to plan how you make up is on a calm day. Pick a pause word, agree how long, and how you come back. Which word would you two pick?

title: Not at 1 AM
old_caption: Some fights are really just two tired people at 1 AM. Caring can sound like: let's talk at breakfast. Then actually show up for breakfast. Save this for your next late-night spiral.

title: You vs. the problem
old_caption: When plans fall apart, it's easy to turn on each other. Move to the same side of the table: it's the two of you against the problem, not against each other. Who's your plan-B person?

title: Keep the point, drop the edge
old_caption: You can be right about the point and still owe a sorry for the volume. Apologize for the tone, keep the point, and give them a real chance to hear what mattered to you.

title: Hold first, fix later
old_caption: When someone you love is hurting, a five-step plan can feel like homework. Ask first: do you want help, or a hug? Then follow their lead.

title: Not in front of everyone
old_caption: A jab in front of everyone lands twice as hard. If it stung, you can say so calmly and save the real conversation for later, just the two of you.

title: Your partner, not a jury
old_caption: Friends are there to support you, not to vote on your partner. The disagreement belongs to the two people in it, so start by talking to each other.

title: Go first with your part
old_caption: Waiting for them to apologize first can turn a small mistake into a standoff. Name your own part, even a small one. It makes room for them to name theirs.

title: Let it be a tie
old_caption: Not every disagreement needs a winner. If it's about the tinsel, let it be a tie and enjoy the half-and-half tree. Save your energy for what really matters to you both.
